description: First 50 seeds only - testing 'starting well' quality

scoring_criteria.9: Perfect native speech in both languages
scoring_criteria.1-2: Marginal, no one would say this

phrases.english: talking in English
phrases.other: الكلام بالإنجليزية
phrases.notes: Both natural. Arabic uses masdar (verbal noun) which is idiomatic. English gerund phrase is natural.

phrases.english: I want to learn English.
phrases.other: أريد أن أتعلم الإنجليزية.
phrases.notes: Perfect in both languages. Natural Arabic with proper subjunctive structure.

phrases.english: I'd like to be able to guess the whole word in English.
phrases.other: أود أن أستطيع أن أخمن الـ كلمة كاملة بالإنجليزية.
phrases.notes: English is natural but unusual context (guessing whole words?). Arabic has odd spacing 'الـ كلمة' - likely a technical artifact. Should be 'الكلمة كاملةً'.

phrases.english: I have to remember her name before I meet her.
phrases.other: أضطر أن أتذكر اسمها قبل أن ألتقي بها.
phrases.notes: Both natural. 'أضطر' (I'm compelled) is slightly formal but acceptable. English is perfect.

phrases.english: I'm going to learn how to speak.
phrases.other: سوف أقوم بالتعلم كيف أن أتحدث.
phrases.notes: English is fine. Arabic is awkward - 'أقوم بالتعلم' (I will do the learning) is overly formal/textbook-ish. Should be 'سأتعلم كيف أتحدث'. The 'كيف أن أتحدث' is also clunky.

phrases.english: I want to learn how to explain what I mean in English.
phrases.other: أريد أن أتعلم كيف أن أشرح ما أعني بالإنجليزية.
phrases.notes: English is perfect. Arabic has redundant 'أن' after 'كيف' - should be 'كيف أشرح'. Minor issue.

phrases.english: I'm going to try to speak the whole sentence in English.
phrases.other: سوف أقوم بالمحاولة أن أتحدث الـ جملة كاملة بالإنجليزية.
phrases.notes: English is fine. Arabic is very awkward - 'أقوم بالمحاولة' is textbook-ish; should be 'سأحاول'. Also 'الـ جملة' spacing issue.

phrases.english: Do you want to be quiet before you speak with me?
phrases.other: هل تريد أن تكون هادئًا قبل أن تتحدث معي؟
phrases.notes: Both grammatically correct. Semantically unusual - asking someone if they want to be quiet before speaking is odd. Could be context-specific.

phrases.english: I'd like to learn how to speak English as often as possible.
phrases.other: أود أن أتعلم كيف أن أتحدث الإنجليزية بقدر الإمكان.
phrases.notes: Semantically odd in both - you don't learn 'how to speak as often as possible', you learn to speak and then practice often. Arabic has redundant 'أن' after 'كيف'.

phrases.english: I'd like to speak English as hard as I can with you.
phrases.other: أود أن أتحدث الإنجليزية بأقصى ما أستطيع معك.
phrases.notes: English 'as hard as I can' with speaking is unusual - 'as much as I can' would be more natural. Arabic is acceptable though slightly formal.

phrases.english: I'm trying to learn how to say something now.
phrases.other: أنا أحاول أن أتعلم كيف أن أقول شيئًا الآن.
phrases.notes: English is natural. Arabic has redundant 'أن' after 'كيف', but otherwise good.

phrases.english: I wouldn't like to be able to speak English after you finish.
phrases.other: لا أود أن أستطيع أن أتحدث الإنجليزية بعد أن تنتهي.
phrases.notes: Semantically strange in both - who says they wouldn't want to be able to speak English? Grammatically fine but pragmatically nonsensical.

phrases.english: I'm going to try if I can remember a word in English.
phrases.other: سوف أقوم بالمحاولة إن أستطيع أن أتذكر كلمة بالإنجليزية.
phrases.notes: English is ungrammatical - should be 'try to see if' or just 'try to remember'. Arabic has the awkward 'أقوم بالمحاولة' again and odd conditional structure.

phrases.english: I want to say something in English with you now.
phrases.other: أريد أن أقول شيئًا الإنجليزية معك الآن.
phrases.notes: English 'with you' is awkward here - 'to you' would be better. Arabic is MISSING 'بـ' - should be 'شيئًا بالإنجليزية'. Grammar error.

phrases.english: I want to be able to explain what I mean in English.
phrases.other: أريد أن أستطيع أن أشرح ما أعني بالإنجليزية.
phrases.notes: Both natural. Standard usage in both languages.

phrases.english: I can explain what I mean in English with you.
phrases.other: أستطيع أن أشرح ما أعني بالإنجليزية معك.
phrases.notes: English 'with you' at end is slightly awkward but acceptable. Arabic is natural.

phrases.english: I'm going to speak a little English with someone else.
phrases.other: سوف أقوم بالتحدث قليلًا من الإنجليزية مع شخص آخر.
phrases.notes: English is natural. Arabic 'أقوم بالتحدث' is formal/textbook-ish; 'سأتحدث' better. 'قليلًا من' is acceptable but 'قليلًا' alone would be more natural.

phrases.english: I speak English now. I want to practise.
phrases.other: أنا أتحدث الإنجليزية الآن. أريد أن أتدرب.
phrases.notes: Both natural. Simple, clear sentences.

phrases.english: I want to practise speaking a little English as often as possible.
phrases.other: أريد أن أتدرب على التحدث قليلًا من الإنجليزية بقدر الإمكان.
phrases.notes: English is slightly long but natural. Arabic is good, though 'قليلًا من' could be simplified.

phrases.english: I like feeling as if I'm nearly going to start talking.
phrases.other: أحب الشعور وكأنني تقريبًا سأبدأ بالكلام.
phrases.notes: Both natural but somewhat unusual semantically. English grammar is fine. Arabic is good.

phrases.english: I'm not sure what's going to be after today.
phrases.other: لست متأكدًا ما سيكون بعد اليوم.
phrases.notes: English is slightly awkward - 'what's going to happen after today' would be more natural. Arabic is fine.

phrases.english: Because I'm nearly ready to go with everyone else.
phrases.other: لأنني تقريبًا جاهز للذهاب مع الجميع.
phrases.notes: Both natural. Simple and clear.

phrases.english: I like to go with people who speak English.
phrases.other: أحب أن أذهب مع أشخاص يتحدثون الإنجليزية.
phrases.notes: Perfect in both languages. Natural and clear.

phrases.english: I want to be quiet before I speak.
phrases.other: أريد أن أكون هادئًا قبل أن أتحدث.
phrases.notes: Both natural. Could imply wanting to gather thoughts before speaking.

phrases.english: I don't like to go
phrases.other: لا أحب أن أذهب
phrases.notes: Both natural as fragments. Would need context to be complete sentences.

phrases.english: I wanted to go
phrases.other: أردت أن أذهب
phrases.notes: Both natural. Good simple past structure.

phrases.english: I want to speak English when I am ready.
phrases.other: أريد أن أتحدث الإنجليزية عندما أكون مستعدًا.
phrases.notes: Perfect in both. Natural and grammatically correct.

phrases.english: I'm not sure if I can speak the whole word now.
phrases.other: لست متأكدًا إن أستطيع أن أتحدث الـ كلمة كاملة الآن.
phrases.notes: English is semantically odd - you don't 'speak a word', you 'say' or 'pronounce' it. Arabic has the 'الـ كلمة' spacing issue.

phrases.english: I'm going to practise speaking English as hard as I can today.
phrases.other: سوف أقوم بالتدرب على التحدث الإنجليزية بأقصى ما أستطيع اليوم.
phrases.notes: English 'as hard as I can' with speaking is unnatural - 'as much as I can' better. Arabic has formal 'أقوم بالتدرب' structure.

phrases.english: I want to be able to say the whole sentence in English today.
phrases.other: أريد أن أستطيع أن أقول الـ جملة كاملة بالإنجليزية اليوم.
phrases.notes: English is fine. Arabic has 'الـ جملة' spacing issue but is otherwise acceptable.

phrases.english: I think that it's a good thing to make mistakes because I don't worry.
phrases.other: أعتقد أن أنه من الجيد أن ترتكب أخطاء لأنني لا أقلق.
phrases.notes: English logic is slightly off - usually 'because I don't worry about them'. Arabic has redundant 'أن أنه' (double 'that').

phrases.english: I want to practise speaking English after now.
phrases.other: أريد أن أتدرب على التحدث الإنجليزية بعد الآن.
phrases.notes: English 'after now' is ungrammatical - should be 'from now on'. Arabic 'بعد الآن' means 'anymore' (negative context) or 'from now on', but the structure is odd.

phrases.english: I wanted to ask you what the answer is.
phrases.other: أردت أن أسألك ما هي الإجابة.
phrases.notes: Perfect in both languages. Natural indirect question.

phrases.english: I speak a little English with you now.
phrases.other: أنا أتحدث الإنجليزية قليلًا معك الآن.
phrases.notes: English is acceptable but 'I'm speaking' would be more natural for current action. Arabic is good.

phrases.english: tonight I wanted
phrases.other: الليلة أردت
phrases.notes: Both are incomplete fragments. Grammatically fine as fragments but need completion.

phrases.english: She doesn't want to read anything this afternoon.
phrases.other: لا تريد أن تقرأ أي شيء بعد الظهر.
phrases.notes: Both natural. Arabic drops subject pronoun (acceptable in context). 'بعد الظهر' = this afternoon, correct.

phrases.english: I want to learn how to say something.
phrases.other: أريد أن أتعلم كيف أن أقول شيئًا.
phrases.notes: English is natural. Arabic has redundant 'أن' after 'كيف'.

phrases.english: I'm trying to remember how to say something in English.
phrases.other: أنا أحاول أن أتذكر كيف أن أقول شيئًا بالإنجليزية.
phrases.notes: English is natural. Arabic has redundant 'أن' after 'كيف', otherwise good.

phrases.english: I'm trying to be able to speak English as often as possible.
phrases.other: أنا أحاول أن أستطيع أن أتحدث الإنجليزية بقدر الإمكان.
phrases.notes: English is awkward - you don't 'try to be able', you 'try to' do something. Arabic mirrors the awkwardness.

phrases.english: I'm not sure if I can guess what I mean now.
phrases.other: لست متأكدًا إن أستطيع أن أخمن ما أعني الآن.
phrases.notes: Semantically odd - you wouldn't 'guess what you mean'. Both languages grammatically fine but pragmatically strange.

phrases.english: I want to speak English with you now.
phrases.other: أريد أن أتحدث الإنجليزية معك الآن.
phrases.notes: Perfect in both languages. Natural and clear.

phrases.english: Because I have to learn English easily soon.
phrases.other: لأنني أضطر أن أتعلم الإنجليزية بسهولة قريبًا.
phrases.notes: English is awkward - 'have to learn easily' is odd; you don't 'have to' do something easily. Arabic mirrors this awkwardness.

phrases.english: He doesn't want to speak
phrases.other: هو لا يريد أن يتحدث
phrases.notes: Both natural as fragments. Complete grammatically.

phrases.english: interrupt the story
phrases.other: نقاطع القصة
phrases.notes: Both natural as verb phrases. Arabic uses 1st person plural which is an interesting choice.

phrases.english: I want to learn how to say the whole sentence in English.
phrases.other: أريد أن أتعلم كيف أن أقول الـ جملة كاملة بالإنجليزية.
phrases.notes: English is natural. Arabic has redundant 'أن' after 'كيف' and the 'الـ جملة' spacing issue.

phrases.english: She doesn't want to remember anything when she is here.
phrases.other: لا تريد أن تتذكر أي شيء عندما تكون هنا.
phrases.notes: Both natural. Slightly unusual semantically but grammatically fine.

phrases.english: I want you to learn
phrases.other: أريدك أن تتعلم
phrases.notes: Perfect in both. Natural causative structure.

phrases.english: I'm looking forward to you to show me how to speak English better.
phrases.other: أتطلع لأن تريني كيف تتحدث الإنجليزية أفضل.
phrases.notes: English is UNGRAMMATICAL - should be 'I'm looking forward to you showing me'. Arabic has issues too - 'كيف تتحدث' should be 'كيف أتحدث' (how I speak, not how you speak).

phrases.english: I don't like feeling as if I'm nearly ready to go.
phrases.other: لا أحب الشعور وكأنني تقريبًا جاهز للذهاب.
phrases.notes: Both natural. Interesting emotional expression.

phrases.english: I'm going to try to learn with someone else in English.
phrases.other: سوف أحاول أن أتعلم مع شخص آخر بالإنجليزية.
phrases.notes: Both acceptable. English word order slightly awkward - 'in English' placement is unusual.

worst_3_phrases.english: I'm looking forward to you to show me how to speak English better.
worst_3_phrases.other: أتطلع لأن تريني كيف تتحدث الإنجليزية أفضل.
worst_3_phrases.reason: CRITICAL: English is ungrammatical - 'looking forward to you to show' is wrong. Should be 'looking forward to you showing me' or 'looking forward to your showing me'. Arabic also has a semantic error - 'كيف تتحدث' means 'how YOU speak' when it should be 'how I speak' (كيف أتحدث).

worst_3_phrases.english: I wouldn't like to be able to speak English after you finish.
worst_3_phrases.other: لا أود أن أستطيع أن أتحدث الإنجليزية بعد أن تنتهي.
worst_3_phrases.reason: SEMANTIC: Pragmatically nonsensical in both languages. Who would say they DON'T want to be able to speak English? Grammatically fine but no realistic use case.

worst_3_phrases.english: I'm going to try if I can remember a word in English.
worst_3_phrases.other: سوف أقوم بالمحاولة إن أستطيع أن أتذكر كلمة بالإنجليزية.
worst_3_phrases.reason: GRAMMAR: English 'try if I can' is ungrammatical - needs 'try to see if' or 'try to remember'. Arabic has awkward formal structure 'أقوم بالمحاولة' and odd conditional framing.

recurring_issues.recommendation: Remove 'أن' - Arabic says 'كيف أقول' not 'كيف أن أقول'
Use simple verb forms: 'سأحاول' not 'سأقوم بالمحاولة'
Technical fix needed - remove space between ال and noun

recurring_issues.issue: English 'as hard as I can' with speaking
recurring_issues.recommendation: Use 'as much as I can' for frequency/effort with speaking
